comments.author: @ledacedar6253
comments.text:
As if everyone isn't fully prepared and follows the weather and tides, when you live remotely. WE are well prepared, with chain saws in the back of everyone's vehicles. When the ferry is blocked from delivering food everyone hits the two grocery stores on Haida Gwaii to grab all the TP, Butter, Cream and milk they can. If your too slow, too bad.
Prince Rupert gets way more rain there, but not so much on Haida Gwaii. Buddy got it wrong- They have been able to prove at least 14,000 yrs of existence...likely more rainbows on HG from all the mist, the Japanese currents that surround the east coast all brings moderate weather and temps. 
But we had one huge dump of beautiful snow one year. Fall trees are a dreary brown, no colours. 

There is a legend of twin giants who lived on the large hill/mountain like at Tow Hill, the name of one giant who threw his brother off the mtn one day in a fight. They also tell of 5 tsunami's. Oral history is fantastic.
Oh-SOY-Yous is the phonetic pronunciation.

comments.author: @documentearth
comments.text: While spending the last few weeks researching and putting together 4K footage on Tristan da Cunha, the detail that blew my mind the most wasn't just the lack of an airport—it’s how the 240 residents in Edinburgh of the Seven Seas still share just 9 family surnames and rely on a single morning harbor gong to decide their entire day. Even after the 1961 volcano eruption forced them to England, 148 of them voted to leave modern life behind and sail 7 days back into the Roaring Forties. Truly the most fascinating community on Earth.

replies.author: @ledacedar6253
replies.text:
Hell look at Haida Gwaiians who live north of VI and it's 6hr ferry trip to get there , if the weather is good! 4,000 people live there and it is definitely Haida Territory, ensuring a rooted cultural experience amidst the live Indigenous culture thriving. They feel desperate from & distinct from Canada, will say their going off to Canada when they leave the Islands, and all who contribute when there are welcome are welcomed Gwaiians. respectful relationships matter. This is a still developing strong and healthy nation that's always been Haida and not FN or aboriginal. Anyone there will tell you that. The population is untied as well.

The Humpback whales come to HG every year in March, for a month. The come into Skidegate Bay every morning and every night leave the bay to go into deeper ocean. They scrub off the barnacles, visit the elders who live right along the shoreline and honour them. I had a patio sitting on the north  end of the bay, and could watch their dark bodies diving deep and then rising to blow, breathe and flip their tales...It was FANTASTIC.
